display.purpose: The page name. Exactly one per page; scales with the viewport instead of wrapping.

headline.purpose: Top-level division inside a markdown page.

title.purpose: Third and fourth heading level; drops to quiet ink at the sixth rather than shrinking further.

body.purpose: The sentence under the name and every paragraph, held to a 34rem measure.

code.purpose: Monospace on the sunken surface, inline at 0.9em and 0.85rem in blocks.

title-xs.purpose: Fifth and sixth heading level; the sixth drops to quiet ink instead of shrinking further.

label.purpose: Table text — the only step below body size that is not code.

components.name: Page Name
components.description: The one display heading a page carries; scales between 2.5rem and 4rem with the viewport.
components.css: .ds-display { margin: 0 0 0.5rem; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: clamp(2.5rem, 8vw, 4rem); font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: -0.02em; line-height: 1.6; color: var(--text, #1a1a18); }

components.name: Lead Sentence
components.description: The single sentence under the page name, and the shape of every paragraph.
components.css: .ds-body { margin: 0; max-width: 34rem; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: clamp(1.05rem, 2.5vw, 1.25rem); line-height: 1.6; color: var(--muted, #5c5c56); }

components.name: Inline Code
components.description: Code inside a sentence: sunken surface, small radius, no border.
components.html: Set APP_NAME to name the page.
components.css: .ds-code-inline { font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.9em; background: var(--surface, #f1f1ee); padding: 0.15em 0.35em; border-radius: 4px; }

components.name: Code Block
components.description: A fenced block on the sunken surface, scrolling within itself, with the four syntax tones.
components.html:
# every service shares one image
services:
  amber:
    ports: 8080
    name: "my site"
components.css: .ds-code-block { margin: 0; padding: 0.9rem 1rem; background: var(--surface, #f1f1ee); border-radius: 6px; overflow-x: auto; font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.85rem; line-height: 1.5; color: var(--text, #1a1a18); } .ds-tok-comment { color: var(--code-comment, #6b6b61); font-style: italic; } .ds-tok-string { color: var(--code-string, #7a5230); } .ds-tok-keyword { color: var(--code-keyword, #6a4a86); } .ds-tok-number { color: var(--code-number, #2b6660); }

components.name: Ruled Table
components.description: Ruled, never boxed; a block-level scroll container so an over-wide table scrolls inside itself.
components.css: .ds-table { display: block; width: max-content; max-width: 100%; overflow-x: auto; border-collapse: collapse; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 0.95rem; } .ds-table th, .ds-table td { padding: 0.5rem 0.7rem; text-align: left; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line, #dededa); } .ds-table th { font-weight: 600; color: var(--text, #1a1a18); } .ds-table td { color: var(--muted, #5c5c56); }

components.name: Quote
components.description: Set aside by a hairline stroke on the left, never by a background tint or a quotation glyph.
components.html: A placeholder has no business in a search index.
components.css: .ds-quote { margin: 0; padding-left: 1rem; border-left: 3px solid var(--line, #dededa); font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; font-style: italic; color: var(--muted, #5c5c56); } .ds-quote p { margin: 0; }

components.name: Secondary List
components.description: Reads as one block of secondary text rather than a stack of separate lines.
components.css: .ds-list { margin: 0; padding-left: 1.4rem; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; color: var(--muted, #5c5c56); line-height: 1.6; } .ds-list li + li, .ds-list li > ul { margin-top: 0.35rem; } .ds-list ul { padding-left: 1.4rem; }

components.name: Text Link
components.description: Carries the surrounding colour; only the underline changes on hover.
components.html: Written up in the readme.
components.css: .ds-link { color: inherit; text-decoration-color: var(--muted, #5c5c56); text-underline-offset: 0.2em; } .ds-link:hover { text-decoration-color: currentColor; } .ds-link:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid currentColor; outline-offset: 2px; }

narrative.overview:
A notice that does not press. It says what there is to say and then stops — no countdown, no invitation to sign up, no rhetoric of anticipation. The page exists because a domain resolves somewhere before its real site does, and its whole ambition is to make that moment unembarrassing. Everything in the system follows from that: one column, no chrome, no motion, nothing to click but the links the operator wrote.

The material is paper rather than screen. Every neutral leans warm — the background is off-white rather than white, the text near-black rather than black — so the page reads as a printed card someone left on the table, not as an interface that happens to be empty. Depth comes from tone and a hairline, never from a shadow. Type is whatever the visitor's device already has, which means the page appears complete on the first paint and looks native on every platform instead of importing a personality from a font file.

Two things the page must never resemble were named explicitly. It is not a maintenance or error screen: nothing here is broken, it is only not there yet, so there is no warning glyph, no apology, no grey-on-grey. And it is not a developer surface: no terminal window, no monospace headings, no green-on-black. The visitor is a visitor, not an operator.
keyCharacteristics: One centred column, at most 34rem wide, on an otherwise empty field
Warm neutrals only; colour appears exclusively inside code
Flat by construction — no shadow anywhere in the system
System type at every level, no web font, nothing fetched at render time
Both colour schemes are first-class; neither is the afterthought

rules.name: The Warm Paper Rule
rules.body: No pure white and no pure black, in either scheme. Every neutral carries a warm cast; a cool grey reads as software and breaks the material.

rules.name: The Four Tones Rule
rules.body: Code gets exactly four colours. A highlighter emits sixty token classes; anything not in the four groups keeps body colour. Adding a fifth means arguing why the page needs it more than it needs quiet.

rules.name: The Measured Contrast Rule
rules.body: Whenever a colour changes, its contrast against its own ground is measured in both schemes and held at or above 4.5:1. The lowest value in the system today is 4.76 (comment on sunken surface, light). No colour ships on the assumption that it looks fine.

rules.name: The Borrowed Type Rule
rules.body: Only fonts the device already has. No web font, no @font-face, no preconnect — the page must render complete with the machine offline.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: One family for everything except code. A second display face would make the page an identity; it is a notice.

rules.name: The One Column Rule
rules.body: Everything lives in one column of at most 34rem. No sidebar, no grid, no second region — a placeholder that needs a layout has stopped being a placeholder.

rules.name: The Content Scrolls, Not The Page Rule
rules.body: Anything that cannot fit — a wide table, a long code line — scrolls inside its own box. The document itself never scrolls horizontally, at any width.

rules.name: The Flat Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow, no filter: drop-shadow, no layered card. If something needs to read as separate, it changes tone or gains a hairline.

rules.name: The Visible Focus Rule
rules.body: Every focusable element shows a focus ring in the current text colour. The ring is never removed to tidy up a layout, and it is never traded for a colour change alone.

dos: Do measure contrast in both schemes whenever a colour changes; hold 4.5:1 or better.
Do keep min-width: 0 on the column — it is what makes the scroll rules work at all.
Do express a new distinction with tone, weight or space before reaching for a colour.
Do let wide content scroll inside its own box.
Do treat both colour schemes as equally finished; test the dark one before shipping.
Do give every focusable element a visible :focus-visible ring in the current text colour.
donts: Don't add a shadow, a boxed card, or an outlined container.
Don't load a web font, an icon set, or any asset from the network.
Don't introduce an accent colour outside the four code tones.
Don't make it look like a maintenance or error screen — no warning glyph, no apology, no grey-on-grey.
Don't make it look like a developer surface — no terminal frame, no monospace headings.
Don't add motion, a hero image, or anything that asks for attention.
